item.title: Reform of the ‘Ownerless’ Election Commission: Audit by the Board of Audit and Inspection or an Independent Evaluation Committee? (‘주인 없는’ 선관위 개혁…감사원 감찰이냐, 독립 평가위냐)
item.description:
The National Election Commission (NEC) was established in 1963 as an independent constitutional body to prevent ‘government-managed elections’ following the fraudulent March 15, 1960 election, which sparked the April 19 Revolution, and has since contributed to the development of South Korean democracy. However, the shortage of ballot papers during the June 3 local elections has amplified calls for fundamental reform of the ‘63-year NEC system.’ The NEC’s long-standing freedom from external oversight and control has been cited as a cause of this incident, leading to outbursts in the political sphere on the 17th about the need for constitutional amendments and even dissolution-level reforms. Yet, given the constitutional spirit and historical context that guarantee the NEC’s independence, some argue that issues should be resolved through measures such as making the NEC chairperson a full-time position and establishing an independent audit body within the NEC, rather than amending the constitution. (중앙선거관리위원회는 4·19 혁명 도화선이 된 1960년 3·15 부정선거 이후 ‘관권선거’를 막자는 취지로 1963년 헌법상 독립기구로 설립된 뒤 한국 민주주의 발전에 기여해왔다. 그러나 6·3 지방선거 투표용지 부족 사태로 ‘63년 선관위 체제’의 근본적인 수술이 필요하다는 목소리가 높아지고 있다. 중앙선관위가 그동안 외부 감시와 통제에서 벗어나 있던 것이 이번 사태의 원인으로 지목되며 17일 정치권에선 개헌 필요성과 더불어 해체 수준의 개혁이 필요하다는 주장이 분출한다. 다만 선관위의 독립성을 보장한 헌법 정신과 역사적 맥락을 고려하면 개헌보다 중앙선관위원장 상임화와 중앙선관위 내 독립 감사기구 설치 등을 통해 문제를 풀어야 한다는 주장도 있다.)

On the day of the local elections (the 3rd), the Songpa-gu Election Commission in Seoul recognized the ballot paper shortage around 11:40 a.m. that day and notified the Seoul Metropolitan Election Commission, but the responsible staff member at the Seoul commission did not report it to the standing commissioner or the secretary general. It wasn’t until after 5 p.m. that same day that the severity of the situation was recognized, and a response was initiated jointly with the NEC. Citizens are questioning the very existence of the NEC, the 17 metropolitan and provincial election commissions, and the 255 municipal, county, and district election commissions, which have starkly revealed a structure that is powerless in crisis response and where no one takes responsibility. (지방선거 당일(3일) 서울 송파구 선관위는 투표용지 부족을 그날 오전 11시40분께 인지하고, 서울시 선관위에 알렸지만 서울시 선관위 담당 직원은 상임위원이나 사무처장에게 보고하지 않았다. 같은 날 오후 5시가 넘어서야 사태의 심각성을 인지하고 중앙선관위와 함께 대응에 나섰다. 국민들은 위기 대응에 무력하고 누구도 책임지지 않는 구조라는 걸 적나라하게 보여준 중앙선관위와 17개 시·도 선관위, 255개 시·군·구 선관위의 존재 의미를 묻고 있다.)

First, experts point out that the current structure, where eight of the nine NEC commissioners, including the chairperson, hold non-standing positions, needs to be changed. Chang Young-soo, a professor at Korea University Law School, noted, “The biggest reason the entire NEC has become an organization with lax discipline is that it has been operated like an ‘ownerless company.’” He added, “Could non-standing commissioners, who have their own primary jobs, have properly grasped the overall work of the NEC? The significance and depth of their decisions have weakened, and the overall management and supervision of the organization have become inadequate.” This suggests the need to expand the number of standing commissioners who can dedicate themselves to election management duties and take responsibility. (먼저 전문가들은 위원장 포함 9명의 선관위원 중 8명이 비상임직인 현행 구조를 바꿔야 한다고 지적한다. 장영수 고려대 법학전문대학원 교수는 “선관위 전체가 기강이 해이한 조직이 돼버린 가장 큰 이유는 ‘주인 없는 기업’처럼 운영됐다는 것”이라며 “본업이 있는 비상임 선관위원들이 선관위 전체 업무를 제대로 파악했겠느냐. 이들이 한 결정의 의미나 깊이가 약해지고 조직 전체의 관리·감독이 부실하게 됐다”고 지적했다. 선거 관리 업무에 전념하고 책임을 질 수 있는 상임위원 확대가 필요하다는 것이다.)

Making the NEC chairperson and metropolitan/provincial election commission chairpersons full-time positions is being discussed as an alternative. However, at a forum hosted on the 17th by the Democratic Party of Korea’s ‘Task Force for Electoral System Reform,’ Jeong Tae-ho, an emeritus professor at Kyung Hee University Law School, stated, “The key challenge is not whether to make the chairperson a full-time position, but how to strengthen the expertise and accountability of the secretariat.” He proposed, “How about appointing a secretary general or standing commissioner who can objectively examine the organization?” (중앙선관위원장과 시·도 선관위원장 상임화가 대안으로 거론된다. 다만 더불어민주당 ‘선거제도 개혁 태스크포스(TF)’가 17일 주최한 토론회에서 정태호 경희대 법학전문대학원 명예교수는 “위원장의 상임화 여부보다 사무처의 전문성과 책임성을 어떻게 강화할 것인가가 중요한 과제”라며 “객관적으로 (조직을) 들여다볼 수 있는 사람으로 사무총장이나 상임위원을 위촉하는 것은 어떻겠나”라고 제안했다.)

Currently, both the ruling and opposition parties argue that fundamental problem-solving requires institutional reforms to allow the Board of Audit and Inspection (BAI) to conduct performance audits on the NEC or enable external oversight. To this end, the Democratic Party and the People Power Party are raising the need for a constitutional amendment explicitly making the NEC—a constitutional institution independent from the executive, legislative, and judicial branches—subject to BAI audits. (현재 여야 모두 근본적인 문제 해결을 위해 중앙선관위도 감사원의 직무감찰을 받거나 외부 감시가 가능하도록 하는 제도적 개혁이 필요하다는 주장을 하고 있다. 이를 위해 민주당과 국민의힘은 헌법상 행정부, 입법부, 사법부로부터 독립된 헌법기관인 선관위를 감사원의 감사 대상으로 명시하는 개헌 필요성을 제기한다.)

Currently, the BAI can only conduct financial audits on the NEC, not performance audits. When the BAI attempted a performance audit in May 2023 over allegations of preferential hiring by the NEC, the NEC filed a competence dispute with the Constitutional Court, which ruled in February that the BAI’s audit was unconstitutional. The court determined that it had infringed on the NEC’s independence. The constitutional fence designed to prevent specific regimes or political forces from exerting influence, in order to block government-managed elections, has paradoxically become a ‘shield’ for the NEC. (현재 감사원은 중앙선관위에 대해 회계감사 외에 감사를 할 수 없다. 감사원이 2023년 5월 선관위의 채용 특혜 의혹에 직무감찰을 하자 선관위는 헌법재판소에 권한쟁의심판을 청구했는데, 헌재는 지난 2월 감사원의 감사가 위헌이라고 판단했다. ‘선관위의 독립성을 침해했다’는 판단이다. 관권 선거를 막기 위해 특정 정권, 정치세력이 영향을 끼칠 수 없도록 한 헌법의 울타리가 역설적으로 선관위의 ‘방패’가 된 것이다.)

However, there are considerable concerns that amending the constitution and shaking the NEC’s independence could leave it vulnerable to influence from the ruling government in the future. At the Democratic Party’s TF forum, Professor Jeong pointed out, “The BAI, being a constitutional institution under the president, leaves open the risk of being misused as a means to infringe on the NEC’s independence.” There is concern that if the ruling power affects the NEC through audit or personnel powers, the foundation of democracy could be shaken. In response, Professor Jeong suggested alternatives such as establishing an independent election management evaluation committee, institutionalizing regular reports to the National Assembly, reporting election incidents, and legislating obligations for preventing recurrence. Kim Kyu-beom, head of the NEC branch of the National Government Employees’ Union, told The Hankyoreh, “If we come under audit by the BAI, which is under the president, the NEC cannot be free from the president. Even if the NEC undergoes audits, such concerns must be resolved.” (그러나 개헌을 통해 선관위의 독립성을 흔들 경우 앞으로 정권의 입김에 휘둘릴 수 있다는 우려도 만만치 않게 나온다. 민주당 티에프 토론회에서 정 명예교수는 “감사원은 대통령 소속 헌법기관이라는 점에서 선관위의 독립성을 침해하는 수단으로 악용될 위험을 배제할 수 없다”고 지적했다. 집권세력이 감사권이나 인사권을 통해 선관위에 영향을 미칠 경우 민주주의의 근간이 흔들릴 수 있다는 우려다. 이에 정 명예교수는 독립적인 선거관리평가위 설치, 국회에 대한 정기 보고의 제도화, 선거 사고 보고, 재발 방지 의무 법제화 등을 대안으로 제시했다. 김규범 국가공무원노조 선관위지부 위원장은 한겨레에 “대통령 아래 있는 감사원의 감사를 받게 되면 대통령으로부터 선관위가 자유로울 수 없다. 선관위가 감사를 받더라도 이런 우려가 해소돼야 한다”고 했다.)

Meanwhile, there are strong voices calling for urgent improvements in election management capabilities and the electoral affairs model, alongside structural reforms. In particular, improving the NEC’s crisis response system, which has proven powerless in emergencies, is crucial. Lee Joon-han, a professor of political science and diplomacy at Incheon National University, told The Hankyoreh, “The NEC needs a system like a ‘five-minute standby team’ that can receive accurate reports and respond swiftly and orderly when unexpected incidents occur.” There are also proposals to introduce a method of printing ballot papers for regular voting, similar to early voting, to prevent a recurrence of the ballot paper shortage. (한편 구조개혁과 더불어 선거관리 역량 강화와 선거사무 모델 개선이 시급하다는 목소리도 크다. 특히 비상 상황에 무력한 선관위의 위기 대응 체계 개선도 중요하다. 이준한 인천대 정치외교학과 교수는 한겨레에 “돌발 상황이 생기면 정확한 보고를 받고 대처를 일사불란하게 할 수 있는 ‘5분 대기조’ 같은 체계가 선관위에 있어야 한다”고 했다. 투표용지 부족 재발을 막기 위해 본투표도 사전투표처럼 투표용지를 인쇄하는 방식을 도입해야 한다는 주장도 나온다.)

Jung Hye-min jhm@hani.co.kr Ko Kyung-joo, Staff Reporter goh@hani.co.kr (정혜민 jhm@hani.co.kr 고경주 기자 goh@hani.co.kr)

item.title: Noh Tae-ak, Overseas Trips with Wife…'Companion' Omitted (노태악, 아내와 선관위 해외 출장…‘동반 사실’ 누락)
item.description:
Former National Election Commission (NEC) Chairman Noh Tae-ak was confirmed to have taken three overseas business trips accompanied by his spouse during his tenure. <<> According to documents submitted by the NEC to Democratic Party of Korea lawmaker Yang Bu-nam on the 17th, former Chairman Noh brought his spouse on three overseas trips during his time in office. These included: an 8-night, 9-day trip to Australia and New Zealand in 2022; a 7-night, 9-day trip to Germany and Estonia in 2024; and an 8-night, 10-day trip to Denmark and Sweden in 2025. The airfare and accommodation costs for former Chairman Noh's spouse on these trips were all covered by taxpayer money. These three trips were official business trips aimed at gathering opinions on election and political systems, evaluating overseas elections, developing election systems, enhancing international networks, and fostering exchanges and cooperation with foreign election management bodies. <<> However, the NEC did not disclose the fact that the spouse accompanied the chairman in publicly released reports. The 2024 overseas trip plan for Germany and Estonia listed only five NEC employees, including former Chairman Noh, as travelers. Similarly, the 2025 trip plan for Denmark and Sweden also omitted the name of former Chairman Noh's spouse. This has raised suspicions that the NEC intentionally concealed the spouse's accompaniment to avoid criticism of budget waste. <<> Allegations of the trips being pleasure-oriented have also emerged. For example, the Denmark and Sweden trip was purportedly aimed at exploring ways to develop the election system by observing local foreign elections, but the schedule for the day after arrival consisted solely of laying flowers at a Korean War memorial. Critics also argue that the local officials former Chairman Noh—ranked 6th in the national protocol order—met with were only working-level staff, which was below his status. Lawmaker Yang criticized, "Neglecting core election management duties while arranging couple's trips under the guise of 'overseas institutional exchanges' is a clear case of pleasure-oriented privilege and a waste of taxpayers' hard-earned money." <<> The NEC explained, "As the head of a constitutional institution, it was necessary to consider treatment commensurate with the position and role, so the budget for the spouse was allocated from the planning stage," adding, "We followed precedent, but going forward, we will operate in line with public expectations." Regarding the omission of the spouse's name from the reports, the commission cited that she was not a public official. <<> Reporter Shim Woo-sam wu32@hani.co.kr (노태악 전 중앙선거관리위원장이 재임 기간 동안 3차례 배우자와 동반 해외 출장을 다녀온 것으로 확인됐다.)

item.title: Legal Professionals: "Nationwide Re-run Election Lacks Requirements, Realistically Impossible" (법조인들 “전국 재선거론, 요건 미비 현실적 불가”)
item.description:
As Jang Dong-hyuk, leader of the People Power Party, repeatedly advocates for a nationwide re-run election, political scholars and legal professionals point out that it is realistically impossible. (장동혁 국민의힘 대표가 연일 ‘전국 재선거론’을 주장하는 가운데 정치학자들과 법조인들은 현실적으로 불가능하다고 지적했다.)

Article 224 of the Public Official Election Act states, "Even if there is a violation of election-related regulations, invalidation of all or part of the election or invalidation of the election of a candidate shall be decided or adjudicated only when it is recognized that it affected the outcome of the election." In other words, a re-run election is possible only if it is acknowledged that the missing ballots could have changed the winner—meaning that if all voters who were unable to vote in the ballot paper shortage had voted, the winning candidate might have changed. (공직선거법 224조는 “선거에 관한 규정에 위반된 사실이 있는 때라도 선거의 결과에 영향을 미쳤다고 인정하는 때에 한하여 선거의 전부나 일부의 무효 또는 당선의 무효를 결정하거나 판결한다”고 돼 있다. 투표용지 부족 사태 탓에 투표를 못 한 유권자가 모두 투표했을 때 당선자가 바뀔 가능성이 인정돼야 재선거가 가능하다는 것이다.)

However, in the June 3 local elections for the Seoul mayoral race, the vote gap between Oh Se-hoon of the People Power Party and Jeong Won-oh of the Democratic Party of Korea was 60,259 votes. On the 9th, the National Election Commission disclosed in data submitted to Rep. Jeong Hee-yong of the People Power Party that the total number of missing ballot papers across Seoul was 4,206. The likelihood of the Seoul mayoral election result changing is thus extremely slim. However, proportional representation elections for metropolitan and basic council members with narrower vote margins could potentially be subject to a re-run election. (그런데 6·3 지방선거 서울시장 선거에서 오세훈 국민의힘 후보와 정원오 더불어민주당 후보의 득표 차는 6만259표였다. 중앙선거관리위원회는 지난 9일 정희용 국민의힘 의원에게 낸 자료에서 서울시 전체에서 부족했던 투표용지 수는 4206장이라고 밝혔다. 서울시장 선거 결과가 바뀔 가능성은 희박한 셈이다. 다만, 표 차이가 적은 광역·기초의원 비례대표 선거는 재선거가 결정될 가능성도 있다.)

Even if a re-run election were held, how to handle both regular voting and early voting also poses a problem. (재선거를 한다고 해도 본투표와 사전투표를 어떻게 할지도 문제다.)

If only the regular voting is re-conducted because the ballot shortage occurred solely during regular voting, the voter turnout might drop. Even if early voting is included, holding a re-run election in only certain areas would make it difficult for voters residing outside those areas to cast absentee early ballots, leading to issues of 'violation of voting rights.' Lee Jun-seok, leader of the Reform Party, wrote on Facebook on the 16th, "It would be problematic if the solution brought up to address the violation of voting rights paradoxically reduces the total number of votes cast. Representative Jang's call for a full-scale re-run election cannot lead to a fair election, no matter which direction it takes." (본투표에서만 투표용지 부족 사태가 있었다고 해서 본투표만 다시 하면 투표율이 떨어질 수 있다. 사전투표까지 같이 시행한다고 해도, 일부 지역만 재선거를 하면 그 외 지역에 나가 있는 유권자는 관외 사전투표가 어려워져 ‘참정권 침해’ 문제가 발생한다. 이준석 개혁신당 대표는 지난 16일 페이스북에 “참정권 침해를 해결하기 위해 들고나오는 해법이 오히려 총 투표수가 줄어드는 역설이면 곤란하다”며 “장 대표의 전면적 재선거는 어느 쪽으로 가도 공정한 선거가 될 수 없다”고 했다.)

Choi Jang-jip, an emeritus professor at Korea University and a veteran political scholar, said to *The Hankyoreh*, "Even if some people had their voting rights infringed upon due to the ballot shortage, those who already voted followed proper procedures, and the results came out. It is problematic to ask these people to vote again." Kim Jun-woo, secretary-general of Lawyers for a Democratic Society, stated, "Even if the court decides on a re-run election, it would likely narrow the scope to only the affected polling stations for regular voting." (원로 정치학자인 최장집 고려대 명예교수는 한겨레에 “(투표용지 부족 사태로) 참정권이 침해된 사람이 있어도, 이미 투표했던 사람은 정당한 절차를 다 밟아서 투표해서 결과가 나왔다. 그런데 이런 사람들까지 다시 다 투표하라는 건 곤란하다”고 말했다. 민주사회를 위한 변호사모임 사무총장 김준우 변호사는 “법원이 만약 재선거를 결정하더라도 가장 범위를 좁혀서, 본투표에 한해 그 (문제가 발생한) 투표구에 한해서만 할 것”이라고 말했다.)

Jang Dong-hyuk's mention on the 9th of "proposing a special law for conducting a re-run election" also carries constitutional concerns as it would be retroactive legislation. Article 13, Clause 2 of the Constitution stipulates, "All citizens shall not be restricted in their voting rights or deprived of property rights by retroactive legislation." If a re-run election changes the winner, it would result in infringing on the voting rights of the existing winner through retroactive legislation. It is also difficult to find 'fault attributable to the party involved,' which is an exceptional circumstance allowing retroactive legislation. (장동혁 대표가 지난 9일 언급한 “재선거 실시를 위한 특별법 발의”도 소급입법이라 위헌 소지가 있다. 헌법 제13조 제2항은 “모든 국민은 소급입법에 의하여 참정권의 제한을 받거나 재산권을 박탈당하지 아니한다”고 정한다. 재선거로 당선자가 뒤바뀔 경우 기존 당선자의 참정권을 소급입법으로 침해하는 결과를 낳는다. 소급입법 허용의 예외적 사정으로 인정되는 ‘당사자 귀책사유’를 찾기도 어렵다.)

Attorney Lim Jae-sung said to *The Hankyoreh*, "Just like in the past when property rights were deprived through retroactive legislation in the recovery of pro-Japanese assets, retroactive legislation is possible only when there is fault on the part of the party. Since the winners of this election are not at fault, it seems unlikely that the special law would be constitutional." Kim Jun-woo also stated, "Because people who have already exercised their voting rights would be harmed, the special law doesn't make sense." (임재성 변호사는 한겨레에 “과거 친일 재산 환수 때 소급입법으로 재산권을 박탈당한 사람들처럼, 당사자에게 귀책사유가 있어야 소급입법 가능성이 있다”며 “이번 선거 당선자들에게 잘못이 있는 게 아니어서 (특별법이 합헌일) 가능성이 없어 보인다”고 말했다. 김준우 변호사도 “이미 참정권을 행사한 사람들이 피해를 보기 때문에 (특별법은) 말이 안 된다”고 말했다.)

Reporter Yoo Young-jae young@hani.co.kr (유영재 기자 young@hani.co.kr)

item.title: "Loser" Resignation Calls Erupt Against Jang Dong-hyuk... People Power Party Files Reelection Appeals for 7 Regions (장동혁 향해 “찌질이” 사퇴론 분출…국힘, 7곳 재선거 소청)
item.description:
On the 17th, after a general meeting of lawmakers, the People Power Party filed election appeals with the National Election Commission and relevant election commissions for a total of 11 regions in connection with the ballot shortage incident during the June 3 local elections. These included seven regions—Seoul, Gyeonggi, Incheon, Busan, Ulsan, Jeonnam/Gwangju, and Chungbuk—filed under the party's name, and four regions—Daejeon, Sejong, Chungnam, and Jeonbuk—filed under the names of candidates. At the meeting, demands for Rep. Jang Dong-hyuk's resignation as party leader erupted, but no conclusion was reached. <<> The People Power Party made this decision regarding the election appeal issue during the general meeting that began around 2 p.m. and lasted over three hours. Rep. Jang argued, "Since we don't know which regions might face issues during the National Assembly's audit of the election commission, let's file election appeals with the central election commission for all 16 metropolitan governments." However, floor leader Rep. Chung Jin-suk reportedly insisted on filing appeals only for the seven regions—Seoul, Gyeonggi, Incheon, Busan, Ulsan, Jeonnam/Gwangju, and Chungbuk—as initially decided by the supreme council meeting. Some lawmakers reportedly questioned, "We won the Seoul mayoral election, so why file an appeal?" After debating the issue for over two hours, the lawmakers decided through a show of hands to file appeals for seven regions. In the vote involving 50 participants, it is known that only two lawmakers—Rep. Park Jun-tae, the party leader's chief of staff, and Rep. Lee Jin-sook—voted in favor of filing appeals for all 16 regions nationwide. Rep. Jang left after staying for about an hour and a half. After the meeting, Rep. Park Jun-tae told *The Hankyoreh*, "We respect the decision of the general meeting, so we filed appeals for seven regions under the party's name and guided candidates to file for four regions on their own behalf." <<> An election appeal is a procedure to challenge the validity of an election or a candidate's victory to the election commission, which must make a decision within 60 days of receiving the appeal. If the election commission accepts the appeal, a reelection is held within 30 days of the decision notification. <<> At the general meeting, there was also heated debate over the issue of Rep. Jang's resignation. Rep. Song Seok-joon requested to make a public statement just before the meeting went into closed session but was blocked, prompting him to say, "There has never been a refusal to allow public statements. In the 22nd National Assembly, our party has completely fallen into a state of non-communication. Isn't that why we've ended up in this worst-case scenario?" Rep. Park Jun-tae shouted back, "If that's the case, go out and (hold a press conference) yourself." <<> During the closed-door meeting, lawmakers including Reps. Song Seok-joon, Kwon Young-jin, Yoon Han-hong, Shin Sung-beom, and Park Hyung-soo, who sat in the front row facing Rep. Jang, urged him to publicly resign. Rep. Song told reporters, "Losing important elections or wars requires boldly taking responsibility and stepping down; that's the essence of a responsible term-based system," adding, "I warned that if he doesn't resign, he won't escape being called a 'loser.'" Rep. Kwon also said, "Proposing a reelection alongside election fraud conspiracy theorists is not an attitude befitting a responsible party." Rep. Park Hyung-soo similarly remarked, "Rep. Jang is already a blunt spear. How can we use that to check President Lee Jae-myung and the Democratic Party's dictatorship?" Rep. Kim Jeong-jae and others urged Rep. Jang not to advocate for a "full-scale reelection." <<> However, Reps. Lee Jin-sook and Kang Seung-gyu spoke against Rep. Jang's resignation. Rep. Park Jun-tae told reporters, "Is the party leader's departure more important than protecting the people's right to vote?" and targeted the party's young-lawmaker group "Alternatives and Future," which demanded Jang's resignation, saying, "If they don't disband, I'll rename them 'Future Without Alternatives.'" <<> Meanwhile, Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon, meeting with reporters before a hearing at the Seoul Central District Court on suspicions of illegal opinion poll cost payments, directly criticized, "The Jang Dong-hyuk leadership has run its course," adding, "The reelection claim is a tactical slogan to strengthen his own political position." <<> Reporter Jang Na-rae wing@hani.co.kr Reporter Cho Hee-yeon choh@hani.co.kr Reporter Yoo Young-jae young@hani.co.kr (국민의힘이 17일 의원총회 뒤 6·3 지방선거 투표용지 부족 사태와 관련해 당 차원에서 서울·경기·인천·부산·울산·전남광주·충북 7곳, 후보자 명의로 대전·세종·충남·전북 4곳 등 총 11곳에 대해 중앙선거관리위원회와 각급 선관위에 선거소청 접수를 신청했다. 의총에서는 장동혁 대표를 향한 사퇴 요구가 빗발쳤으나 결론을 내지 못했다.)

item.title: President Lee Calls on Trump to Be "Peacemaker" for Korean Peninsula… Trump Responds "I Will" (이 대통령 “한반도 피스메이커” 요청…트럼프 “하겠다” 화답)
item.description:
President Lee Jae-myung, currently on a visit to Europe, requested U.S. President Donald Trump on the 16th (local time) to "play a constructive role as a peacemaker for the substantive resolution of issues on the Korean Peninsula." In response, President Trump said, "I will fulfill the necessary role." <<> During an official dinner hosted by French President Emmanuel Macron and his wife on the sidelines of the Group of Seven (G7) summit in Évian-les-Bains, President Lee met with President Donald Trump and stated, "We hope for continued attention and engagement to establish sustainable peace on the Korean Peninsula, following the Middle East," according to Deputy National Security Advisor Oh Hyun-joo on the 17th. In response, President Trump expressed a strong commitment, saying, "I will do what is necessary to advance the Korean Peninsula issue," and added, "I will explore ways to contribute to peace on the Korean Peninsula and will communicate closely with President Lee," Deputy Advisor Oh reported. <<> Deputy Advisor Oh added, "President Trump assessed President Lee as a 'strong leader,' and both leaders expressed expectations that they could jointly contribute to peace and security on the Korean Peninsula." She also noted, "The two leaders agreed on the importance of South Korea-U.S.-Japan cooperation, based on a robust South Korea-U.S. alliance." President Lee sat next to President Trump at the official dinner and conversed for about two hours. <<> The South Korean and U.S. leaders also exchanged views on the U.S.-Israel vs. Iran war, which is approaching a ceasefire phase. <<> Deputy Advisor Oh said, "The two leaders concurred on the importance of free and safe navigation in the Strait of Hormuz," and added, "They shared expectations that the restoration of stability and peace in the Middle East would stabilize oil prices and lead to economic recovery." It was reported that President Lee conveyed his congratulations on the successful conclusion of the U.S.-Iran ceasefire negotiations, particularly on President Trump's birthday. <<> Discussions also touched on the "Iran reconstruction fund." The U.S. financial daily *Financial Times* reported on the 15th that the U.S. is considering creating a $300 billion (approximately 454 trillion won) fund for Iran's reconstruction. A key official from the presidential office stated, "President Lee expressed that South Korea has the will and capability to substantially contribute to the efforts of the entire international community, including the U.S., to ensure free and safe navigation in the Strait of Hormuz in the future." <<> On the same day, President Lee also engaged in defense sales during a summit with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney. He told Prime Minister Carney, "South Korea, as a defense powerhouse, is ready to actively contribute to strengthening Canada's security capabilities based on trust." South Korea's Hanwha Ocean is competing with Germany's Thyssenkrupp Marine Systems (TKMS) for a contract in Canada's next-generation submarine project, valued at up to 60 trillion won. On the 17th, before the start of the second session of the expanded G7 summit meeting, President Lee held a brief 10-minute meeting with Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. President Lee will conclude his European tour with a South Korea-Kenya summit and a working luncheon of the summit meeting, returning home on the 18th. <<> Évian-les-Bains / Reporter Seo Young-ji yj@hani.co.kr (유럽을 방문 중인 이재명 대통령이 16일(현지시각) 도널드 트럼프 미국 대통령에게 “한반도 문제의 실질적 해결을 위해 피스메이커로서 건설적 역할을 해달라”고 요청했다. 이에 트럼프 대통령은 “필요한 역할을 다하겠다”고 답했다.)

item.title: Foreign Election Commissions Under Parliamentary/Government Control… Monitoring Structures Despite Independence Guarantees (외국 선관위 의회·정부 통제 받아…독립성 보장에도 감시구조 갖춰)
item.description:
South Korea’s National Election Commission is explicitly defined as an independent body under the Constitution, ensuring high independence, but it effectively lacks parliamentary oversight or external audits. In contrast, most foreign election management bodies guarantee independence while maintaining structures where parliaments or external audit agencies monitor and control budgets, personnel, and performance. (한국의 선거관리위원회는 헌법상 독립기구로 명시된 만큼 독립성이 높지만, 의회 감독이나 외부 감사가 사실상 없다. 반면 국외 선거관리기관은 독립성을 보장하되, 의회나 외부 감사기구가 예산·인사·성과 등을 감시·통제하는 구조를 갖춘 경우가 대부분이다.)

According to the International Institute for Democracy and Electoral Assistance (International IDEA)’s “Comparative Report on Election Management Bodies by Country” (2014) and the National Election Commission’s “2024 Comparative Study of Election Management Bodies in Various Countries,” election management bodies are broadly classified into three types: independent, governmental (where a body under the executive branch manages elections), and mixed (where an independent body and an executive body jointly manage elections). Independent types include South Korea, Australia, and Canada; governmental types include Germany, the United Kingdom, and the United States; and mixed types include France and Japan. ( 17일 국제민주주의선거지원연구소(International IDEA)의 ‘국가별 선거관리기관 비교 보고서’(2014), 중앙선거관리위원회의 ‘2024년도 각국의 선거관리기관 비교연구’ 보고서를 보면, 선거관리기관은 크게 독립형, 행정부형(행정부 소속 기구가 선거 관리), 혼합형(독립기구와 행정부 기구가 함께 선거 관리)으로 나뉜다. 독립형은 한국·오스트레일리아(호주)·캐나다, 행정부형은 독일·영국·미국, 혼합형은 프랑스·일본 등이다.)

Most countries, regardless of the status of their election management bodies, have external monitoring structures. Election management bodies in independent-type countries such as India, South Africa, and Kenya are constitutional independent bodies with very high independence and legal status, but they still undergo parliamentary oversight or audits by audit institutions. ( 대부분의 국가는 선거관리기구의 위상과 상관없이 외부 감시 구조를 갖추고 있다. 독립형인 인도, 남아프리카공화국, 케냐 등의 선거관리기관은 헌법상 독립기구로 독립성과 법적 지위가 매우 높지만 의회 감독이나 감사원 감사 등을 받는다.)

Governmental and mixed-type election management bodies face strong control from parliaments and governments. In the United Kingdom, a committee chaired by the Speaker of the House of Commons reviews the election commission’s budget proposal and five-year plan. It also undergoes financial and performance audits by the National Audit Office (NAO) under Parliament. In Germany, the head of the Federal Statistical Office concurrently serves as the Federal Returning Officer, subject to financial audits by the Federal Court of Auditors, with an obligation to report on whether issues noted during audits have been corrected. In France, the Ministry of the Interior directly handles election administration, and like other administrative bodies, it undergoes financial and performance audits by the Court of Audit. ( 행정부형·혼합형 선거관리기관은 의회와 정부의 강한 통제를 받는다. 영국은 하원 의장이 주재하는 위원회가 선관위 예산안과 5개년 계획을 심사한다. 의회 소속 국가감사원(NAO)으로부터 재무 감사와 성과 감사도 받는다. 독일은 통계청장이 연방선거관리관을 겸임하는데 연방감사원 재정 감사를 받고, 감사 당시 지적 사항을 시정했는지 보고할 의무가 있다. 프랑스는 내무부가 직접 선거행정을 담당해 다른 행정기관과 마찬가지로 회계감사원으로부터 재무 감사와 성과 감사를 받는다.)

Meanwhile, unlike South Korea, where the chairman of the National Election Commission is a non-standing position, in most countries such as Canada, Australia, and the United Kingdom, the head of the election management body holds a standing position. ( 한편, 선거관리위원장이 비상임직인 우리와 달리 캐나다, 오스트레일리아, 영국 등 대부분의 국가는 선거관리기관장이 상임직이다.)

Reporter Goh Kyung-ju goh@hani.co.kr ( 고경주 기자 goh@hani.co.kr)
